summary: First full test run for DentisTree microsite (backend + frontend). All 13 backend pytest tests pass (100% success). Frontend loads with correct branding, hero, header, all sections, sticky bar responsive behaviour, hero WhatsApp booking flow (modal -> POST /api/bookings persisted -> window.open wa.me link) all working. Sticky bar hidden on desktop and visible on mobile as expected. Real dentistree.me images all return 200. One real UI bug found: Gallery lightbox close button (data-testid=lightbox-close-btn) is not clickable because the sticky <header> intercepts pointer events over the top strip of the viewport.

ui_bugs.issue: Close button (lightbox-close-btn) at top-5 right-5 is unreachable — clicks intercepted by <header data-testid='site-header'> (sticky, z-50). Root cause: lightbox is rendered inside <main class='relative z-10'>, which creates a stacking context that caps the lightbox's z-[100] at z-10. Header sits in the outer stacking context at z-50, so it visually and pointer-event-wise sits above the lightbox in the top strip. Escape key also does not close it (no keydown handler). Backdrop click works only in areas below the header.

action_items: Fix gallery lightbox close button — render the lightbox in a React Portal to document.body (recommended), OR move it out of <main> in App.js, OR raise the lightbox above the header by removing the wrapping stacking context.
Add Escape key handler to close the lightbox (UX polish).
critical_code_review_comments: Gallery.jsx lightbox has a stacking-context bug (lightbox inside <main class='relative z-10'> can't rise above sticky header at z-50 even with z-[100]). Use createPortal or lift the modal to <body>.
Gallery lightbox lacks keyboard accessibility (no Escape handler, no focus trap, no aria-modal).

BookingModal.jsx: window.open is called even when the POST /api/bookings request throws — errors are only logged, no user-visible error toast for the persistence failure. Consider showing an error before still opening WhatsApp (or blocking send if persistence fails).
server.py uses deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') hooks — should migrate to lifespan context manager (works today but prints DeprecationWarning).
server.py: CLINIC dict is a module-level constant; consider moving to a config or DB so main agent can update without redeploy.
No pagination or auth on GET /api/bookings — bookings contain PII (name, phone, DOB) and are publicly readable. Add auth or restrict this endpoint before production.

rca_of_the_issue.bug: Gallery lightbox close button not clickable
reproduction_steps: Scroll to Gallery section and click any gallery item (e.g. data-testid='gallery-item-0').
Click the close button (data-testid='lightbox-close-btn') at top-right.

Nothing happens. Playwright reports: '<header data-testid=site-header> intercepts pointer events'. Pressing Escape also does not close it. Only clicking the backdrop in the lower portion of the screen (below the header row) closes it.
rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: Gallery.jsx renders the lightbox as a sibling <div class='fixed inset-0 z-[100] ...'> inside <section id='gallery'>, which lives inside <main class='relative z-10'> in App.js. Because <main> is positioned with an explicit z-index, it creates a new stacking context; every descendant (including the lightbox with z-[100]) is capped at z:10 relative to the root. The <Header> component (sticky, z-50) sits OUTSIDE <main>, so it stacks above the entire main subtree including the lightbox. Result: the top strip of the viewport is owned by the header and eats all pointer events, making the close button unreachable.
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: Preferred fix: render the lightbox via ReactDOM.createPortal(..., document.body) so it escapes the <main> stacking context. Alternate fixes: (a) move the lightbox JSX to App.js (outside <main>) and lift `active` state up; (b) remove z-10 from <main> (may cause other layering issues); (c) hide the header when a lightbox is open. Additionally add a useEffect keydown listener for Escape and aria-modal / focus trap for accessibility.
